checked_items.item: Insulation-coordination logic for the pad voltage rating
checked_items.evidence: Agent compares the TSP 3500 4000 Vac ASTM D149 breakdown (a destructive 60 Hz rms value) with a 2.5 kV impulse peak ('1.6x'); breakdown is not a withstand rating and rms-vs-impulse is not the IEC 60664-1 procedure. standards_safety.json treats the requirement as a 4 kV basic impulse and calls 4 kVac 'no margin', recommending the thicker grade or a 6 kV class pad. The two agents conflict.

knowledge_misuse: KR-TH-003 is a human-review rule; the 90 / 100 / 110 degC thresholds and the T_J mapping are presented as design values in selection and pcb_constraints while knowledge_used says they were 'surfaced, not decided' - label them as review proposals in the hardware/firmware contract.

SKILL-006 procedure step 3 (films and magnetics out of the exhaust) is an AIPE recommendation without source evidence; the agent applies it as fixed >= 20 / >= 30 mm distances without labelling the distances as recommendations.

The copper-width method is the IPC-2221 formula (k = 0.048 / 0.024, exponents 0.44 / 0.725); calling it 'IPC-2152-style' misattributes it. KR-PCB-006 is a low-confidence single-reference rule, which the agent handled correctly by adding its own sizing method.

KR-TH-002 verification requires checking the interface voltage rating; the agent's check compares an ASTM D149 breakdown (rms) with an impulse peak, which is not the insulation-coordination logic the standards agent applies (4 kV impulse view) - the conflict must be preserved for human review rather than resolved by the thermal agent's '1.6x' statement.

Reference instance values (TI 40 degC, 0.5 and 0.1 degC/W) were correctly not copied; the applicability of SKILL-006 (forced air, TO-247 on sinks) and KR-TH-001 (heat-sinked semiconductors) is satisfied.

summary: Every calculation in the thermal result reproduces from its stated inputs (conduction re-check, required R_th,HS, T_J for the three sinks and two pads, KR-TH-001 P_max, fan-fail steady state and time to trip, pad resistance, pressure, capacitance, NTC divider and mapping, IPC-2221 widths, copper loss, inductor/exhaust rises, time constants), the shared-sink model is physically correct, TI instance values were not copied and human-review rules were surfaced. The result is nevertheless incomplete or inconsistent in several engineering respects: the HS device is hottest at 360 V / 27.5 A (T_J,HS 132.2 degC max R, 137.6 degC with a 40 N clip), not at 440 V; the 0.80 K/W pad value assumes 60 N clips, the top of the agent's own range; the inductor placeholder (6-10 W) contradicts the inductor agent's 16-18 W toroid; the 185 x 60 x 55 mm envelope and 0.68 K/W contradict the architecture's 110 x 50 mm reservation and 0.6 K/W target; the NTC ring lug cannot physically sit between the devices at 28 mm pitch with 28 mm pads; the 90 degC derate threshold lies below the legal steady-state sink temperature with max-R parts and the 100 degC trip margin collapses to 3.5-4.4 K with the fan at 10.8 V; the pad voltage-rating logic (D149 breakdown vs impulse) conflicts with the standards agent's 4 kV view; and the fan is missing from the aux 12 V budget. The hard constraint KR-TH-001 (T_J <= 150 degC) holds in every recomputed corner (worst 137.6 degC), so the verdict is confirmed with the listed corrections; the 125 degC preference is met only with typical parts and 60 N clips, and the D K upgrade is the robust resolution of most findings. All Fischer LAM 5 figures remain search-snippet level (RS snippet corroborates 0.68 K/W for LAM 5 100 12; the K / 12 V variant pages were blocked).
